newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet, to finalise deal by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Stet, to finalise deal by year-end.

text.p: Italian telecom holding Stet and U.S. computer giant IBM will finalise a global communications deal by the end of the year, Stet managing director Ernesto Pascale told a parliamentary hearing.

Stet and IBM announced a preliminary deal to combine backbone networks in a 50/50 joint venture in August 1995, but talks to complete the negotiations were rapidly bogged down and many analysts believed the project would be called off.

The aims of the accord are believed to have changed since the original announcement and Pascale said earlier this year that the Italian and U.S. companies were looking for another European partner to join the planned venture.
"Our policy is orientated towards operations that can support much wider alliances...with a partner willing to take on the role of global operator," Pascale told parliament.
"Talks are in process. By the end of the year we will reach an accord with IBM," he told the lower house of parliament's transport commission.
The IBM/STET alliance was expected to involve a broad range of computing networking, information technology and voice and data services offered to clients worldwide.
Recent media reports said IBM was now looking at cooperating with STET's Finsiel systems integration unit in a venture which would involve outsourcing IT services.

Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported earlier this month that the planned agreement could be of a commercial nature, while share swaps, which appeared possible a year ago, were no longer on the agenda.
